summary.allegation: The cardholder says Roastline Coffee Co charged their card twice for GBP 54.00 on 12 April 2025 and that only one purchase was made, so the second GBP 54.00 charge is a duplicate.
summary.to_defend: Visa requires evidence that the two charges were two separate purchases, with documentation of each purchase event and the timestamp and authorisation code for each charge.

requirements.title: Two separate purchases
requirements.text: Evidence the two transactions are for two separate purchases (e.g. different order IDs, different items, different services rendered).
requirements.finding: The merchant supplied two invoices with different invoice numbers and order IDs (RL-88291 / RL-ORDER-44188 and RL-88294 / RL-ORDER-44192) containing entirely different goods: coffee beans in the first order and an Aeropress kit plus filter papers in the second. The two baskets coincidentally total GBP 54.00 each after a GBP 6.00 loyalty discount on the first.

requirements.title: Each purchase documented
requirements.text: Documentation of each purchase event (separate invoices, separate delivery confirmations, separate service dates).
requirements.finding: Each purchase event is separately documented: two dated invoices to the same customer J. Patel at N1 4PD, each with its own delivery date and its own DPD consignment number (7711224488 delivered 14 April, 7711224501 delivered 15 April).

requirements.title: Timestamps and auth codes
requirements.text: Transaction timestamps and authorisation codes for each charge.
requirements.finding: Both invoices state a distinct capture timestamp and a distinct authorisation code: 442189 captured 12 Apr 2025 08:11:33 and 552781 captured 12 Apr 2025 19:42:18, roughly eleven and a half hours apart. The first matches the disputed transaction txn_5523IJ recorded at 2025-04-12T08:11:33Z.

alerts.text: D1 states capture at 08:11:33 BST while the transaction record shows 2025-04-12T08:11:33Z (UTC), a one hour difference in the labelled clock time; confirm which charge (auth 442189 or 552781) is the one being disputed as txn_5523IJ.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

checks.label: Key evidence comes from document text, not only from an image
Images the evidence relies on are fully legible
Every quoted passage was found in the documents
The rule check and the AI recommendation agree

justification: Represent: R1, R2 and R3 are all satisfied, with two distinct order IDs, separate deliveries and two different authorisation codes showing the charges were separate purchases, not a duplicate.
rationale:
The cardholder claims two GBP 54.00 charges on 12 April 2025 were a duplicate of a single purchase.
The merchant evidences two separate orders the same day: RL-ORDER-44188 (coffee, invoice RL-88291) at 08:11 and RL-ORDER-44192 (Aeropress kit and filter papers, invoice RL-88294) at 19:42.
Each charge carries its own authorisation code, 442189 and 552781, captured about eleven and a half hours apart.
Each order was shipped separately on its own DPD consignment, 7711224488 delivered 14 April 2025 and 7711224501 delivered 15 April 2025, to the cardholder's billing address N1 4PD.
The matching GBP 54.00 totals are coincidental, the first basket being GBP 60.00 less a GBP 6.00 loyalty discount, so the charges are not duplicates.
